# Owned PMA reference inputs

Plaintexts and generator code are project-authored under the repository license. No upstream test archive, user file, original program or emulator source is imported into Git. Reference programs remain under `build/toolchain/`, outside product dependency closures, with their original licenses and terms. The [wire contract](../../../docs/engineering/pma-streams.md) discloses source observations separately from independent byte comparisons.

## References

- Yoshihiko Mino's [original PMarc 2.00 package](https://www.asahi-net.or.jp/~am9y-mn/arc/pmarc200.pma), SHA-256 `e735229dc938358230af86c74235fb4b358dfdd9012b1311816371798a30d294`. Its extracted, unmodified `PMARC2.COM` is 10368 bytes, SHA-256 `28aa664d70d6c464d459a7e2db8be5b2a22d62d4d41485e5acd58f27b7ce32da`. The [original CP932 manual](https://www.asahi-net.or.jp/~am9y-mn/doc/pmarc2.doc) SHA-256 is `1dbedd35b21bc7131b67631d9ff180c1bfe9d2547e86b24cfbeeff7aeb04575f`.
- Original PMext 2.22 in Wolverine Logan's documented 1997 IBM-PC port. The [published package](https://hansotten.file-hunter.com/uploads/files/pmarcpc.zip) SHA-256 is `668a81cc3d77eee41255874812a543ac28d4adf9991f04e5d48bcbe1d7fdbff5`; its `PMEXT.CPM`, 12928 bytes, SHA-256 `5d4c0cf8b10c2ed4fa27998bcaabec7018139da5ca31fee0d1c36c96073a1f9e`, remains unmodified. These original proprietary tools retain their author terms, including the original noncommercial-use condition; they are not redistributed with fixtures or product packages.
- [cpmemu](https://github.com/avwohl/cpmemu/tree/275c977c3b3dd058586f4acf49d467c69fcf3969), GPL-3.0, commit `275c977c3b3dd058586f4acf49d467c69fcf3969`. Source zip SHA-256 `c4ec97fe9d5580b20c389d22efdce8d17eee3c7b5af075b68e5f2090c8d27c80`. Only source, license and relevant documentation are extracted, with source bytes checked against that zip before compilation. No CP/M operating-system image or emulator test binary is imported.
- The existing Strawberry Perl 5.42.3.1 C++ compiler, GCC 13.2.0, executable SHA-256 `a30b01810e44edaa465cc51f1dffae6267cb0092cc653d71b881970866039cca`. The owned generator invokes the reference's seven C++ source files with its Windows build settings and deterministic PE timestamp option. Compilation completes before the resulting native executable is hashed and used.
- [Lhasa 0.6.0](https://github.com/fragglet/lhasa/releases/tag/v0.6.0), ISC, Windows executable SHA-256 `93cf8100eb520e49708c5076694253d52caf241d6013be4e37c11ec8e89bbe85`. Complete extracted file bytes are compared, without Windows stdout newline conversion.

The generator uses a fresh owned `build/` child per run, confines the emulated A drive and working directory, clears inherited CP/M device redirections, selects binary file mappings and passes only known names. PMarc encodes `HELLO.BIN`; PMext extracts that member as data, without executable-device or automatic-execution requests. Every process has a timeout. Reference results and generated executable identities remain local artifacts.

## Inputs

Fourteen archives come from the original PMarc encoder. `pm2-boundary-{size}.pma` uses sizes 128, 256, 512, 1024, 2048, 4096, 8192 and 16384. The byte cycle consists of values 0–255 followed by `abracadabra abracadabra\n` repeated 128 times; repeat and truncate that cycle to the named size. `pm2-long.pma` uses the same cycle for 131072 bytes. `pm2-spaces.pma` is 8192 spaces, `pm2-zeros.pma` 65536 zeroes, and `pm2-allbytes.pma` repeats 0–255 to 65536 bytes. These actual compressed members use PM2, without mislabeling the original encoder's Store fallback.

`pm0-allbytes.pma` stores byte values 0–255 using the explicit no-compression option. A zero-length source is skipped by PMarc, so `empty.pma` is an empty archive, one zero byte and 127 `0x1a` bytes, rather than an empty file member. Physical source sizes are multiples of 128 to avoid uncertain CP/M source-record padding. Binary mode prevents text EOF truncation. The original headers preserve `HELLO.BIN` and their actual zero timestamp; the tools are not patched to change metadata.

Two additional wire-authored archives distinguish boundaries outside ordinary compressor choices. `pm2-deep28.pma` has a complete 29-symbol tree with lengths `[28, 1, 2, ..., 27, 28]`, minimum 1 and five-bit length entries. It uses an absent position table and 128 literal-zero symbols, each with the 28-bit canonical code `2^28 - 2` and rank 7. Its output is bytes 39 down to 32 repeated sixteen times, so a wrong tree cannot pass as a constant fill. `pm2-prologue-zero.pma` changes only the leading packed bit of the 512-byte original sample from one to zero. Both have known complete contents and independently corrected framing/CRCs where needed. They are not original-encoder outputs.

Both Lhasa and PMext must exactly read every complete payload, and empty-container results are checked separately. Original CP/M terminator and `0x1a` alignment fill remain part of the owned archive, not its compressed payload. Rust fixture expectations are generated from the original fields and known plaintext CRC, not Rust decoder output. Tests additionally check full plaintexts, exact work/memory/source bounds, mandatory final control events, typed I/O, source-independent cancellation, absent-table use, invalid counts and bounded mutations.

## Reproduction

PM1 has a separate wire-authored set generated by `scripts/generate-pm1-fixtures.py`, without claiming original PMarc 1.24 encoder output. That historical tool source was unavailable. Its wire observations use [Lhasa PM1](https://github.com/fragglet/lhasa/blob/v0.6.0/lib/pm1_decoder.c), Git blob `bb2937e382c8c8a8f5783b94a96b9b59e2c4e74b`, with expanded symbolic alphabets and project-owned content. The generator does not read or invoke the Rust decoder. PMext and Lhasa must both reproduce every complete file before an input is admitted. CP/M output is physically record-padded, so all declared test plaintext lengths are multiples of 128; no prefix-only comparison counts as complete verification.

The PM1 set covers all 32 selectors, both repeated branches of selector 17, every literal/copy length escape, two-byte far copies, position-dependent distance boundaries, history wrap, overlap and a final short literal without a fabricated copy. `pm1-known.bin` concatenates exact owned plaintexts in generated descriptor order; descriptor offsets retain full byte comparisons without reconstructing expectations using the decoder. `pm1-long-overlap.pma` contains 24704 spaces and exercises polling after input is already buffered. The separate check mode verifies reference identities, both readers, each archive, complete known bytes and generated Rust descriptors; reports stay under build.

Run `python scripts/generate-pm1-fixtures.py --check` for the 66 PM1 archives and 134400 complete known bytes. In generated case order, SHA-256 over each UTF-8 archive filename, zero byte and complete archive, then `pm1-known.bin`, a zero byte and its complete content, is `f903b0359a950df4b6df4f85800cc3670681c6187ae333390ad3ef903b7165f2`. This is separate from the original PM0/PM2 set identity below.

Place the fixed references under the directories used by `scripts/generate-pma-fixtures.py`, then run `python scripts/generate-pma-fixtures.py --check`. It verifies reference identities, builds the standalone CPU/BDOS test host, independently regenerates archives and compares every byte plus the exact Rust expectations. Without `--check`, it replaces only these owned inputs. No reference component becomes a product runtime dependency. Reports go under `build/review/format-expansion/`.

For all 16 archive files sorted by UTF-8 filename, SHA-256 of each filename, a zero byte and complete archive bytes concatenated in that order is `df253fd3cdb37337bd6fa25d6cebbc22fee69c287b04b38ab225237f959763f3`. Check mode compares this identity, every archive and the exact generated expectations.
